# Example Output — GitHub Actions Scheduled Automation

*Generated by applying the GitHub Actions Scheduled Automation skill to `example-input.md`.*

---

## 1. Trigger plan

| Trigger | Role | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| External dispatcher (cron-job.org, free tier) | **primary** | 06:00, 09:00, 17:00 UTC — starts within seconds |
| Repo `schedule` | backup only | same three times, 10 minutes later so it no-ops when the dispatch already ran |
| `workflow_dispatch` | manual, with a `force` input | on demand |
| `issue_comment` | approvals | on comment |

The repo crons stay, but they are now the fallback rather than the mechanism — the guard makes a double-fire harmless.

## 2. Dispatch setup

```text
POST https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/workflows/pipeline.yml/dispatches
Authorization: Bearer <fine-grained-pat>
{"ref":"main","inputs":{"slot":"discover"}}        → 204 No Content
```

PAT: fine-grained, **this repository only**, Actions read and write, 90-day expiry with a calendar reminder. Stored in the scheduler, nowhere else.

## 3. Guard logic

State file `state/<date>.json` is the source of truth for "already done".

- The guard runs for **every** trigger, not just `schedule` — this is what the manual test bypassed.
- `discover` is skipped when today's state exists, unless `inputs.force == true`.
- `publish` is made idempotent instead of guarded: it records `published_at` per slot in the same state file and exits 0 if that slot is already marked. An extra 17:00 dispatch is now a no-op rather than a second post.

Verified: running the dispatch twice in a row produced one API call and one post.

## 4. Secret matrix

| Job | Secrets passed | Startup validates |
|---|---|---|
| `discover` | `SUPABASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | both |
| `publish` | `SUPABASE_URL`, `PLATFORM_TOKEN` | those two only |

`build_context()` takes `needs_llm: bool` and only requires `LLM_API_KEY` when the caller asks for it. The 17:00 failure disappears, and the publish job no longer carries a model credential it has no use for.

## 5. Chatops rules

- Required: `github.event.issue.state == 'open'` **and** author association in `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`.
- Command grammar: `^(approve|reject)\s+pick\s+(\d+)$`, case-insensitive, on a comment of 40 characters or fewer.
- Rejected by the new rules: `closing this off — details in Issue #8` (too long, no grammar match) — the exact comment that published the wrong item.
- Accepted: `approve pick 3`.

## 6. Verification

- Dispatch call returns `204`; run appears in Actions within ~5 seconds.
- Second same-day `discover` dispatch: skipped by the guard, no API spend.
- `force: true` dispatch: runs, and logs that it overrode the guard.
- Replay of the "closing this off" comment: workflow starts, command parser exits 0, nothing published.
- Local push flow now `git pull --rebase origin main` first; `state/*.json` conflicts resolve by taking the remote (bot-written) copy.
